description: The Grade 9 Space Students of GD Goenka Public School, Motihari, are enthusiastic young explorers passionate about astronomy, rockets, satellites, and space technology, developing scientific curiosity, creativity, critical thinking, teamwork, and problem-solving skills through hands-on Space Lab activities, innovative projects, and collaborative learning while aspiring to become future scientists, engineers, and pioneers of India's space exploration journey.
summary:
NASA Expedition Command is a unified, browser-based aerospace mission control and visualization platform built for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 by the RASNAA Challengers.
The platform tackles the challenge of planning safe, sustainable human landings at the lunar south pole by integrating eight mission-critical modules into a single web application: a high-fidelity 3D Moon globe with all 9 NASA Artemis candidate landing sites, a topographic horizon ephemeris with real-time Sun/Earth clearance calculations, a first-person lunar surface sortie simulator with 1/6g gravity, a heliocentric solar system orrery with Mars explorer, a modular rocket staging workshop with live Tsiolkovsky Δv validation, a satellite reconnaissance system with 7 sensor shaders, and an AI-powered astrodynamics copilot (ARIA).
Built entirely with Vanilla JavaScript, Three.js, and HTML5 Canvas — no frameworks, no build tools — it runs fully offline. Its scientific rigor is paramount: all calculations are transparently classified as [CALCULATED], [ESTIMATE], or [SIMULATION], grounded in IAU selenographic frames, LOLA altimetry data, and Keplerian orbital mechanics. The platform empowers mission planners to compare, rank, and visualize candidate sites in ways no single prior tool offered.
details:
Exploring the Moon, One Decision at a Time

1. What does your project do and how does it work?

Our project, ApexBuild, is a web-based platform that allows users to explore the Moon and understand how scientists and space agencies plan lunar missions.

We wanted to create something where people don't just read about the Moon but actually get to explore it. Through our interactive 3D Moon Explorer, users can navigate the lunar surface, explore nine potential landing sites, and examine important details about each location.

We have also developed a site-ranking system that compares landing locations based on four important factors: solar illumination, Earth communication, landing safety, and access to permanently shadowed regions. Users can adjust the importance of these factors and see how their decisions affect the rankings.

Additionally, our platform includes satellite reconnaissance visualizations and a Mission Brief Generator that helps turn a selected location and mission plan into a structured report.

2. What benefits does it have?

One of the biggest benefits of ApexBuild is that it brings different aspects of lunar mission planning together in one place.

Instead of switching between different tools or reading complicated scientific information, users can explore locations, compare their conditions, and understand why certain sites may be more suitable than others.

It also makes space science more interesting and accessible, especially for students who want to learn how real space missions are planned.

3. What is the intended impact of your project?

Our main aim is to make lunar exploration easier to understand and encourage more people to take an interest in space science.

As humans prepare for future Moon missions, choosing the right landing location becomes extremely important. A location must offer scientific opportunities while also meeting practical requirements such as safety, sunlight, and communication.

Through ApexBuild, we want users to experience some of these challenges themselves. We hope our project encourages students to think critically, experiment with different decisions, and develop an interest in aerospace technology.

In the future, we would like to expand the platform with more real scientific datasets, advanced terrain analysis, and realistic mission simulations.

4. What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use?

We developed ApexBuild as a web application using:

  • HTML5 – To build the structure of the website.
  • CSS3 – To design the interface and make it responsive.
  • JavaScript – To handle interactive features, calculations, and mission-planning functions.
  • Three.js / WebGL – To create the interactive 3D lunar environment.
  • GLB 3D Models – To integrate the Moon's three-dimensional model.
  • Visual Studio Code – For writing and managing our code.
  • Google Antigravity – To assist with development and debugging.

The project runs through a web browser and does not require any specialised hardware.

5. How is your project creative?

We didn't want to create another ordinary website filled with information about the Moon. We wanted to build an experience where users could actually participate in the exploration process.

What makes ApexBuild different is the combination of a 3D lunar environment, candidate-site selection, customizable ranking, reconnaissance visualizations, and automatic mission reporting.

We have tried to bring the experience of a mission-control environment into a platform that is simple enough for beginners to use.

The idea is simple: instead of just telling someone how a lunar mission works, let them explore, make decisions, and understand the process themselves.

6. What factors did your team consider?

While developing ApexBuild, we considered several factors that could influence the success of a lunar mission:

  • Solar Illumination: How much sunlight is available for power generation and surface operations?
  • Earth Communication: How easily can a lunar landing site communicate with Earth?
  • Landing Safety: Are the terrain, elevation, and slopes suitable for a safe landing?
  • Scientific Importance: Does the location offer opportunities for meaningful scientific research?
  • Permanently Shadowed Regions: Could nearby shadowed regions provide opportunities to investigate water ice?
  • User Experience: Can someone without technical knowledge easily understand and use our platform?
  • Technical Feasibility: Can the platform run smoothly on commonly available devices?
  • Future Development: Can we add more scientific data and advanced features as the project grows?

Our Vision

ApexBuild started with one simple idea: make lunar exploration more interactive and understandable.

As a team, we wanted to combine technology, creativity, and space science to build something that goes beyond a traditional educational website.

We know there is still a lot we can improve, but this project is our step towards exploring how technology can help people understand the challenges of future lunar missions.

We don't just want people to look at the Moon. We want them to explore it, question it, and think about what it takes to reach it.

Project Website: https://apexbuild.in
